response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len FROM film GROUP BY rating), b AS (SELECT AVG(length) AS base FROM film), s1 AS (SELECT r.rating, r.avg_len FROM r, b WHERE r.avg_len > b.base), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS m1 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.rating, s1.avg_len FROM s1, m WHERE s1.avg_len > m.m1) SELECT AVG(s2.avg_len) AS mean_avg_length, AVG(s2.avg_len - b.base) AS mean_excess_over_baseline, AVG(s2.avg_len - m.m1) AS mean_excess_over_kept_mean FROM s2, b, m

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is the plain average of length over all films with non-null length, not the average of the per-rating averages.

'The kept ratings' mean' is the mean of the average lengths of the ratings that passed the first filter (above baseline). The second filter uses this mean, and the third output column measures excess over it. If it meant the mean of the final remaining ratings, the third column would always be 0.
